chunks.title: deploy-render.yml
chunks.text:
# Redeploys the server on Render whenever the app code changes.
# Uses Render's deploy hook, stored as the repository secret RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK
# (Render dashboard -> yakov-llm -> Settings -> Deploy Hook). Without it, does nothing.
name: Deploy to Render
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["yakovllm/**", "web/**", "Dockerfile"]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Trigger Render deploy
        env:
          HOOK: ${{ secrets.RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$HOOK" ]; then
            echo "RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK is not set; skipping." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          curl -fsS -X POST "$HOOK" > /dev/null
          echo "Render deploy triggered." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

chunks.title: refresh.yml
chunks.text:
# Keeps yakov.LLM in step with GitHub: re-indexes new or changed projects,
# commits the new knowledge base and republishes the demo on GitHub Pages.
name: Refresh knowledge base
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 */6 * * *"          # every 6 hours
  workflow_dispatch:                 # "Run workflow" button
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [project-updated]         # sent by a project's push (see docs/notify-yakov-llm.yml)
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["web/**", "scripts/build_demo.py"]   # republish the demo when the UI changes

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: refresh
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  refresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}   # always the latest main, also on re-runs
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.12" }
      - name: Sync with GitHub (only changed repos are re-indexed)
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: python -m yakovllm.ingest --github "${{ github.repository_owner }}"
      - name: Commit the new knowledge base
        id: commit
        run: |
          if git diff --quiet -- data/kb.json; then
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "No project changed."
          else
            git config user.name "yakov.LLM bot"
            git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            git add data/kb.json
            git commit -m "Update knowledge base from GitHub"
            # main may have moved while we were indexing: replay our commit on top, retry a few times
            for i in 1 2 3; do
              git pull --rebase -X theirs origin "${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}" && git push && break
              sleep 5
            done
            echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Build the static demo
        run: python scripts/build_demo.py
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with: { path: dist }

chunks.title: yakov.LLM
chunks.text:
# yakov.LLM

**עוזר AI שמכיר את כל הפרויקטים שלי ב-GitHub.** שואלים אותו על הקוד, על החלטות התכנון או איך להריץ משהו, ומקבלים תשובה עם הפניה לקובץ ולשורות המדויקות. כשאני מוסיף פרויקט או דוחף שינוי, הוא מתעדכן לבד.

An AI assistant that knows every project in my GitHub account. Ask about the code, the design decisions or how to run something, and the answer cites the exact file and lines. When I add a project or push a change, it updates itself.

**▶ Live app:** https://yakov-ashgar27.github.io/yakov.LLM/ (installable on phone and desktop; search runs in the browser, written answers come from the hosted server)

![Home screen](docs/screenshot-home.png)

## Where to look in the code

- [`yakovllm/search.py`](yakovllm/search.py): BM25 written from scratch, with field weighting, repo focus and per-file diversity.
- [`yakovllm/tokenizer.py`](yakovllm/tokenizer.py): one tokenizer for Hebrew and code. It splits `findPathStep` into its words and strips Hebrew prefixes (ו, ה, ב, ל…).
- [`yakovllm/sync.py`](yakovllm/sync.py): follows a GitHub account and re-indexes only the repos that changed, then swaps the live index without a restart.
- [`web/engine.js`](web/engine.js): the same search engine in JavaScript, so the static demo needs no server. A test checks that both return identical results.
- [`eval/`](eval/): 38 questions with known answers, and the script that scores retrieval.

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › How it works
chunks.text:
## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR GH[(GitHub account)] -->|new or changed repos| SYNC[sync.py
every 30 min / webhook / Action] SYNC --> CH[chunker.py
code, docs, pages
with line numbers] CH --> KB[(data/kb.json)] KB --> IDX[BM25 index
search.py] Q[Question] --> RW[Query rewrite
fast model] RW --> IDX IDX -->|top 6 excerpts| LLM[LLM: Groq, Gemini or Claude
answers with citations] LLM -->|streamed| UI[Chat UI] ``` 1. **Ingest.** Every text file that helps answer questions (source code, Markdown, HTML pages, config) is split into chunks that keep their repo, path and line range. Markdown is split by headings, code into 60-line windows that prefer to end on a blank line, HTML pages into visible text. Each repo also gets an overview chunk with its summary, file types and folders. 2. **Search.** A question is tokenized the same way and scored with BM25. Hebrew words are also mapped to the English words the code uses ("אויב" → `enemy`), because a Hebrew question about English code otherwise shares no words with it. With an API key, a fast model also suggests search keywords and probable function names. 3. **Answer.** The six best excerpts go to the model with the conversation, and the model must cite them as `[1]`, `[2]`. The model is pluggable: Claude, or free options (open models on Groq, Gemini Flash), or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. In the UI each citation opens the cited lines, highlighted, with a link to the same lines on GitHub. 4. **Stay current.** See below. ![A citation opens the exact lines](docs/screenshot-source.png)

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Staying in sync with GitHub
chunks.text:
## Staying in sync with GitHub

There are three ways, and they work together:

| How | When it runs | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Server sync** | Every 30 minutes, and on demand from the projects panel | Set `GITHUB_USER` |
| **Webhook** | Instantly on every push to a repo that has the webhook | Payload URL `…/api/webhook/github`, content type JSON, secret = `WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| **GitHub Action** ([`refresh.yml`](.github/workflows/refresh.yml)) | Every 6 hours, from the Actions tab, or from a push in any project | Nothing. For instant runs, copy [`docs/notify-yakov-llm.yml`](docs/notify-yakov-llm.yml) into a project |

Each sync lists the account's public repos and compares each repo's `pushed_at` time with the stored one. A new repo is cloned and indexed, a changed repo is pulled and re-indexed (only that repo), and a deleted or archived repo is dropped. If GitHub can't be reached, the old index keeps serving.

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Results
chunks.text:
## Results

Retrieval measured on [38 questions](eval/questions.json) (20 in Hebrew, 18 in English) over 5 repos, 238 files and 602 chunks. A question is a hit when the file that holds the answer is in the top results.

| Setup | Hit@1 | Hit@5 | MRR | Hit@5 Hebrew | Hit@5 English | ms/query |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BM25 (plain tokens) | 50% | 79% | 0.60 | 70% | 89% | 0.4 |
| BM25 + Hebrew→English glossary | 53% | **87%** | **0.67** | **85%** | 89% | 0.6 |

The glossary raised Hebrew recall from 70% to 85%. These numbers don't include the model keyword rewrite, which needs an API key at evaluation time. `python eval/run_eval.py` prints the table and lists the misses.

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Run it
chunks.text:
## Run it

Python 3.10+ is all you need, with **no dependencies** to install.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yakov-ashgar27/yakov.LLM && cd yakov.LLM
export GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...              # free written answers (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY)
python -m yakovllm                       # http://localhost:8000
```

Without any key the app still works: answers are the matching excerpts.

| Provider | Key | Cost | Default model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` | Free tier, no card | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` |
| Google Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Free tier | `gemini-flash-latest` |
| Anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Paid | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Any OpenAI-compatible API | `LLM_API_KEY` + `LLM_BASE_URL` | Varies | set `LLM_MODEL` |

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/yakov-ashgar27/yakov.LLM)

On Windows you can double-click `run.bat` instead (it reads `.env`). To use Docker, run `docker build -t yakov-llm . && docker run -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env yakov-llm`. Render deploys `render.yaml` in one click.

To index a different account, run:

```bash
python -m yakovllm.ingest --github <user>          # only new or changed repos
python -m yakovllm.ingest --github <user> --force  # rebuild everything
python -m yakovllm.ingest --local ~/code/my-repo   # local folders
```

Settings are in [`.env.example`](.env.example).

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Tests
chunks.text:
## Tests

```bash
pip install pytest && python -m pytest -q
```

There are 26 tests. They cover the tokenizer, the chunker (line numbers must match the source exactly), BM25 ranking, and GitHub sync against real temporary git repos (add, update, remove, and network failure). They also cover the HTTP API against fake Claude and OpenAI-compatible servers that speak their streaming protocols, webhook signatures, rate limiting, CORS for the static demo, identical Python and JavaScript search results on every evaluation question, and a guard that fails CI if Hit@5 drops below 80%.

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Design decisions
chunks.text:
## Design decisions

- **BM25 instead of embeddings.** The corpus is small, about 600 chunks. Code questions use exact identifiers (`find_path_step`, `RBAC`), where keyword search is strong. BM25 runs in 1 ms with no model download, and it runs in the browser too. Cross-language recall, the usual weakness, is handled by the glossary and the query rewrite. The evaluation set is there to show when embeddings start to pay off.
- **Standard library only.** The server, the model streaming clients and the search engine have no dependencies, so the project runs anywhere and is easy to read end to end.
- **One engine, two runtimes.** The JavaScript port lets the demo work as a single static file. A parity test keeps both runtimes in lockstep.
- **Grounded answers.** The prompt requires a citation for every claim about the projects and an honest "not in the sources". The UI makes each citation one click away from the real lines.

chunks.title: yakov.LLM › Project structure
chunks.text:
## Project structure

```
yakovllm/
  tokenizer.py    Hebrew + code tokenizer, glossary, repo aliases
  chunker.py      files -> chunks with line numbers
  ingest.py       clone/read repos -> data/kb.json
  sync.py         incremental GitHub sync, live index swap
  search.py       BM25 index
  llm.py          streaming clients (Claude, Groq, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible), prompts, offline mode
  server.py       HTTP server: UI, /api/chat (SSE), /api/search, /api/sync, webhook
web/              chat UI (vanilla JS): app.js, engine.js, markdown.js, style.css
eval/             questions.json, run_eval.py
tests/            pytest suite
scripts/          build_demo.py (single-file demo), build_offline_kb.py
.github/workflows ci.yml, refresh.yml (sync + GitHub Pages)
```

## API

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/health` | Mode, model, index size, sync status |
| GET | `/api/repos` | Indexed repos with summaries and last push |
| GET/POST | `/api/search?q=…&repo=…&k=…` | Raw search results with scores and matched terms |
| POST | `/api/chat` | `{messages, repo?}` → Server-Sent Events: `meta` (sources), `delta` (text), `done` |
| POST | `/api/sync` | Check GitHub now (with `SYNC_TOKEN` set, needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) |
| POST | `/api/webhook/github` | GitHub webhook (HMAC-SHA256 verified) |

MIT License · Yakov Ashgar

# One-click deploy on Render (free plan).
# Written answers for free: paste a Gemini key (aistudio.google.com/apikey).
# Other options (set in the dashboard instead): GROQ_API_KEY (free) or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (Claude, paid).

    autoDeployTrigger: commit
    buildFilter:
      paths:
        - yakovllm/**
        - web/**
        - Dockerfile
    envVars:
      - key: GEMINI_API_KEY

      - key: GITHUB_USER
        value: yakov-ashgar27
      - key: SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN
        value: "30"
      - key: WEBHOOK_SECRET

chunks.title: build_demo.py › main
chunks.text:
"""Build the static demo: ONE self-contained HTML file with the knowledge base inside.

    python scripts/build_demo.py            # -> dist/index.html (+ dist/kb.json)
    python scripts/build_demo.py --embedded # no live refresh from GitHub (for sandboxed hosts)

The demo needs no server. Search runs in the browser (web/engine.js); answers
come from Claude when the page is opened inside Claude, otherwise the page shows
the best matching excerpts. GitHub Pages serves this file (see .github/workflows).
"""
import base64
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
WEB = ROOT / "web"
DIST = ROOT / "dist"


def main() -> None:
    html = (WEB / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    kb = (ROOT / "data" / "kb.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    json.loads(kb)  # fail early on a broken file

    def inline_css(m):
        return "<style>\n" + (WEB / m.group(1)).read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\n</style>"

    def inline_js(m):
        return "<script>\n" + (WEB / m.group(1)).read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("</script", "<\\/script") + "\n</script>"

    html = re.sub(r'<link rel="stylesheet" href="([\w.]+)">', inline_css, html)
    html = re.sub(r'<script src="([\w.]+)"></script>', inline_js, html)
    icon = base64.b64encode((WEB / "icon.svg").read_bytes()).decode()
    html = html.replace('href="icon.svg"', f'href="data:image/svg+xml;base64,{icon}"')
    embedded = "--embedded" in sys.argv
    if embedded:  # sandboxed host (an artifact): no manifest, no service worker, no live refresh
        html = re.sub(r'\s*<link rel="manifest"[^>]*>|\s*<link rel="apple-touch-icon"[^>]*>', "", html)
        html = re.sub(r"kbUrl: '[^']*'", "kbUrl: ''", html)
        html = html.replace("window.YAKOV_CONFIG = {", "window.YAKOV_EMBEDDED = true;\n    window.YAKOV_CONFIG = {", 1)
    kb_script = "<script>window.YAKOV_KB = " + kb.replace("</", "<\\/") + ";</script>\n"
    html = html.replace("</head>", kb_script + "</head>", 1)

    DIST.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (DIST / "index.html").write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
    (DIST / "kb.json").write_text(kb, encoding="utf-8")
    if not embedded:  # installable app (PWA) files
        for name in ("manifest.webmanifest", "sw.js", "icon.svg", "icon-192.png", "icon-512.png",
                     "icon-maskable-512.png", "apple-touch-icon.png"):
            (DIST / name).write_bytes((WEB / name).read_bytes())
    print(f"dist/index.html · {len(html.encode()) / 1e6:.1f} MB")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

chunks.title: build_offline_kb.py
chunks.text:
"""Rebuild data/kb.json from local checkouts, with real GitHub push times.

Used where the GitHub API is unreachable (CI sandboxes). Normal use:
    python -m yakovllm.ingest --github yakov-ashgar27
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from yakovllm import ingest  # noqa: E402
from yakovllm.sync import GitHubSync  # noqa: E402

src = Path(sys.argv[1])
meta = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text())  # [{"full_name","pushed_at","homepage",...}]
ingest.list_user_repos_meta = lambda user: [{"description": "", "homepage": "", "stars": 0, **m} for m in meta]
ingest.clone = lambda full: next(p for p in src.iterdir() if p.name.lower() == full.split("/")[1].lower())
GitHubSync(meta[0]["full_name"].split("/")[0], Path("data/kb.json")).check(force=True)

chunks.text:
"""Split source files into chunks that keep their file path and line numbers.

Every chunk remembers where it came from (repo, path, first and last line), so
an answer can cite "bomberman/ai.py lines 24-58" and link straight to GitHub.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

CODE_WINDOW = 60      # lines per code chunk
CODE_OVERLAP = 8      # lines repeated between neighbouring code chunks
MD_TARGET = 1500      # characters per markdown chunk (soft)
MD_MAX = 2400         # a section longer than this is split by paragraphs
HTML_WINDOW = 40

DEF_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?"
    r"(?:def|class|function|const|let|interface|type|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)"
)
HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,4})\s+(.*)")


@dataclass
class Chunk:
    id: str
    repo: str
    path: str
    start: int          # 1-based first line
    end: int            # 1-based last line
    title: str          # heading path for docs, first definition for code
    kind: str           # "doc" | "code" | "page" | "config"
    text: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


def _kind_for(path: str) -> str:
    low = path.lower()
    if low.endswith((".md", ".txt", ".rst")):
        return "doc"
    if low.endswith((".html", ".htm")):
        return "page"
    if low.endswith((".yml", ".yaml", ".toml", ".json", ".ini", ".cfg", ".bat", ".sh")) or low.endswith("dockerfile") or "/dockerfile" in low:
        return "config"
    return "code"


def _strip_html(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Visible text of an HTML page, one output line per input line."""
    joined = "\n".join(lines)
    # Drop script/style bodies but keep their newlines so line numbers stay true.
    joined = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style)\b.*?</\1>", lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n"), joined)
    joined = re.sub(r"(?s)<!--.*?-->", lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n"), joined)
    joined = re.sub(r"<[^>\n]*>", " ", joined)
    joined = html.unescape(joined)
    return [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ln).strip() for ln in joined.split("\n")]

def _chunk_markdown(repo: str, path: str, lines: list[str]) -> list[Chunk]:
    sections: list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]] = []  # (heading path, start line, lines)
    stack: list[str] = []
    cur: list[str] = []
    cur_start = 1
    in_fence = False
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if line.strip().startswith("```"):
            in_fence = not in_fence
        m = None if in_fence else HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            if any(s.strip() for s in cur):
                sections.append((" › ".join(stack), cur_start, cur))
            level = len(m.group(1))
            stack = stack[: level - 1] + [m.group(2).strip().strip("*")]
            cur, cur_start = [line], i
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if any(s.strip() for s in cur):
        sections.append((" › ".join(stack), cur_start, cur))

    # Merge small neighbouring sections; split very long ones by paragraph.
    chunks: list[Chunk] = []
    buf: list[str] = []
    buf_start, buf_title = 1, ""

    def flush(end_line: int) -> None:
        nonlocal buf
        text = "\n".join(buf).strip()
        if text:
            chunks.append(Chunk("", repo, path, buf_start, end_line, buf_title or path, "doc", text))
        buf = []

    for title, start, sec in sections:
        sec_text = "\n".join(sec)
        if len(sec_text) > MD_MAX:
            if buf:
                flush(start - 1)
            # paragraph split, still tracking line numbers
            para: list[str] = []
            p_start = start
            for j, ln in enumerate(sec):
                para.append(ln)
                size = sum(len(x) + 1 for x in para)
                if (not ln.strip() and size >= MD_TARGET) or size >= MD_MAX:
                    buf, buf_start, buf_title = para, p_start, title
                    flush(start + j)
                    para, p_start = [], start + j + 1
            if para:
                buf, buf_start, buf_title = para, p_start, title
                flush(start + len(sec) - 1)

BIDI_RE = re.compile("[\u200e\u200f\u202a-\u202e\u2066-\u2069\ufeff]")


def chunk_file(repo: str, path: str, content: str) -> list[Chunk]:
    content = BIDI_RE.sub("", content)
    lines = content.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").split("\n")
    kind = _kind_for(path)
    if kind == "doc" and path.lower().endswith(".md"):
        chunks = _chunk_markdown(repo, path, lines)
    elif kind == "page":
        chunks = _chunk_lines(repo, path, lines, kind, _strip_html(lines), HTML_WINDOW)
    else:
        chunks = _chunk_lines(repo, path, lines, kind, lines, CODE_WINDOW)
    for i, c in enumerate(chunks):
        c.id = f"{repo}:{path}:{c.start}-{c.end}"
    return chunks

    elif name.lower().endswith(".github.io"):

    else:

        title = h1.group(1).strip() if h1 else name
    summary = ""

def build(paths: list[tuple[Path, str]], out: Path, owner: str = "") -> dict:
    repos, chunks = [], []
    for path, name in paths:
        meta, cs = ingest_repo(path, name)
        repos.append(meta)
        chunks.extend(cs)
    return write_kb(repos, chunks, out, owner)


def write_kb(repos: list[dict], chunks: list[dict], out: Path, owner: str = "") -> dict:
    kb = {
        "version": KB_VERSION,
        "owner": owner or next((r["owner"] for r in repos if r.get("owner")), ""),
        "built_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "repos": repos,
        "tokenizer": {  # shared with web/engine.js
            "stopwords": sorted(tokenizer.STOPWORDS),
            "glossary": tokenizer.GLOSSARY,
            "aliases": tokenizer.REPO_ALIASES,
            "prefix1": "".join(sorted(tokenizer.HE_PREFIX_1)),
            "prefix2": sorted(tokenizer.HE_PREFIX_2),
        },
        "chunks": chunks,
    }
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(kb, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")), encoding="utf-8")
    log(f"wrote {out} · {len(repos)} repos · {len(chunks)} chunks · {out.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")
    return kb

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build the yakov.LLM knowledge base")
    ap.add_argument("--github", metavar="USER", help="ingest every public repo of this GitHub user")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", nargs="*", default=[], metavar="OWNER/NAME", help="specific GitHub repos")
    ap.add_argument("--local", nargs="*", default=[], metavar="DIR", help="local folders (git checkouts)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(DEFAULT_OUT))
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="with --github: re-index every repo, not only changed ones")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if a.github and not a.repo and not a.local:
        from .sync import GitHubSync  # full, incremental GitHub sync
        result = GitHubSync(a.github, Path(a.out)).check(force=a.force)
        print(json.dumps(result))
        if "error" in result:
            sys.exit(1)
        return
    targets: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    for full in a.repo:
        targets.append((clone(full), full.split("/")[-1]))
    for d in a.local:
        p = Path(d).expanduser().resolve()
        targets.append((p, p.name))
    if not targets:
        ap.error("give --github USER, --repo OWNER/NAME or --local DIR")
    build(targets, Path(a.out), owner=a.github or "")


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""BM25 search over the knowledge base, written from scratch (no libraries).

BM25 scores a chunk higher when it contains the query's rare words many times,
and normalises for chunk length. On top of plain BM25 we add three things that
matter for a code + docs corpus:

* field weighting: words in the repo name, file path and section title count
  as if they appeared META_WEIGHT times;
* repo focus: when the question names a project ("in Bomberman ..."), chunks
  from that project get a boost (or a hard filter when the UI picks a project);
* diversity: at most MAX_PER_FILE chunks from one file in the results, so the
  answer can draw on several places.
"""

@dataclass
class Hit:
    chunk: dict
    score: float
    terms: list[str]

    def to_dict(self, n: int | None = None) -> dict:
        c = self.chunk
        d = {k: c[k] for k in ("id", "repo", "path", "start", "end", "title", "kind", "text")}
        d["score"] = round(self.score, 3)
        d["terms"] = self.terms
        if n is not None:
            d["n"] = n
        return d

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "yakov.LLM"

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # quieter logs: method, path, status
        if os.environ.get("QUIET"):

        super().log_message(fmt, *args)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- utils
    def _cors(self):
        """Let the GitHub Pages demo call this API from the browser."""
        origin = (self.headers.get("Origin") or "").rstrip("/")
        if origin and (origin in CORS_ORIGINS or "*" in CORS_ORIGINS):
            self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
            self.send_header("Vary", "Origin")

    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        self.send_response(204)
        self._cors()
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, OPTIONS")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Max-Age", "86400")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
        self.end_headers()

    def _json(self, obj, status=200):
        body = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self._cors()
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _body(self, limit=200_000) -> bytes:
        n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        if n > limit:
            raise ValueError("request too large")
        return self.rfile.read(n) if n else b""

    def _client_ip(self) -> str:
        fwd = self.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For", "")
        return fwd.split(",")[0].strip() or self.client_address[0]

                extra = {k: m[k] for k in ("pushed_at", "description", "homepage", "stars")}
                meta, cs = ingest.ingest_repo(path, name, extra)
                repos[key] = meta
                chunks_by_repo[key] = cs
                result["updated" if old else "added"].append(key)

            for key, r in list(repos.items()):
                if key not in seen and (r.get("owner", "").lower() == self.user.lower() or not r.get("owner")):
                    del repos[key]
                    chunks_by_repo.pop(key, None)
                    result["removed"].append(key)

            changed = any(result.values())
            if changed or not self.kb_path.exists():
                ordered = sorted(repos.values(), key=lambda r: r.get("pushed_at") or r.get("committed_at") or "", reverse=True)
                chunks = [c for r in ordered for c in chunks_by_repo.get(r["key"], [])]
                tmp = self.kb_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
                new_kb = ingest.write_kb(ordered, chunks, tmp, owner=self.user)
                tmp.replace(self.kb_path)
                self.status["last_change"] = time.time()
                if self.on_update:
                    self.on_update(new_kb)
            self.status.update(last_check=time.time(), last_error=None, last_result=result)
            ingest.log(f"sync {self.user}: {result}")
            return result
        except Exception as e:  # network down, rate limit, git error: keep serving the old index
            self.status.update(last_check=time.time(), last_error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            ingest.log(f"sync failed: {e}")
            return {"error": str(e)}
        finally:
            self.status["running"] = False
            self._lock.release()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ background
    def trigger(self) -> None:
        """Ask the background loop to sync now (webhook, UI button)."""
        self._wake.set()

# Changelog

## v1.1.1 (2026-11-15): field-hardening

Every fix below came from running WiFi-Doctor on a real Windows 11 laptop. Each has a regression test.

- **RCA:** a single dropped probe no longer counts as packet loss (minimum 2 lost probes per window).
- **RCA:** rolling windows reset when the chaos mode changes, so back-to-back simulations are diagnosed independently.
- **Stress test:** self-induced load is excluded from incidents and from the learned baseline, and the windows are cleared when the test ends.
- **Stress test:** transfer errors are logged and returned as `diagnostics` when no speed-test endpoint is reachable.
- **Diagnosis:** Wi-Fi remediation no longer repeats the same advice twice. "Wi-Fi" casing is fixed in the physical-layer text.
- **UI:** the chaos panel no longer stretches to the height of the bufferbloat card.
- **Windows launcher** (`scripts/run_local.bat`):
  - repairs a broken session PATH and installs missing tools via winget
  - stops only its own previous instance, never other apps
  - picks free ports when 8000 or 5173 are taken
  - keeps the backend tied to the console window

chunks.title: Changelog › v1.1.0 (2026-11-15)
chunks.text:
## v1.1.0 (2026-11-15)

- **Adaptive anomaly baselines:** a per-hop rolling median/MAD baseline (400 samples) with a robust z-score, combined with the static thresholds (hybrid triggering).
- **Physical Wi-Fi telemetry:** RSSI, band, channel, SSID and PHY rates from `netsh` (locale-tolerant), `iw`, `/proc/net/wireless`, `airport` and `system_profiler`. The data is used as evidence in LOCAL_WIFI diagnoses and shown as a topology badge.
- **Active bufferbloat test:** an 8-second load test that compares loaded and unloaded latency and grades the connection A+ to F. It has a 409 concurrency guard, a 10 s watchdog and an SQM recommendation.

## v1.0.0 (2026-11-15)

- Multi-layer prober (gateway, WAN, DNS) with a scapy → icmp_dgram → ping → TCP fallback chain.
- Deterministic RCA engine with confidence scoring, chaos simulation, a SQLite incident log and an ISP CSV report.
- React + TypeScript + Tailwind NOC dashboard, Docker Compose setup and CI.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Why WiFi-Doctor?
chunks.text:
## Why WiFi-Doctor?

"The Internet is slow" can mean four very different things: a weak Wi-Fi signal, a saturated uplink, a congested ISP, or a slow DNS resolver. Each one has a different fix and a different person to call.

Packet sniffers such as Wireshark show you everything and conclude nothing. WiFi-Doctor works the other way around:

| | Passive sniffers | **WiFi-Doctor** |
|---|---|---|
| Data collection | Captures existing traffic | **Actively probes** each layer of the path every 1.5 s |
| Output | Raw packet tables | **Plain-English diagnosis** + confidence score + fix |
| Correlation | Manual | Latency/jitter/loss **correlated with local bandwidth** automatically |
| Evidence | pcap files | **Timestamped incident log + CSV report** you can send to your ISP |
| Setup | Drivers, admin rights, expertise | Runs unprivileged and **never crashes** when it lacks permissions |

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Why WiFi-Doctor? › Key features
chunks.text:
### Key features

- **Multi-layer active probing**: Gateway (Wi-Fi/LAN) → ISP/WAN (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8` backup) → DNS (real UDP/53 A-record queries).
- **Deterministic RCA engine** with five verdicts (`LOCAL_WIFI`, `BUFFERBLOAT`, `ISP_WAN`, `DNS_SERVER`, `HEALTHY`), each with a confidence score and remediation steps.
- **Rolling-window telemetry math** with NumPy: current, average and P95 RTT, jitter, and packet loss per hop.
- **Adaptive anomaly baselines**: a ~10-minute robust baseline per hop (median + MAD) yields a z-score, so a jump from 12 ms to 60 ms is caught on *your* network even though it is below every static threshold.
- **Physical Wi-Fi telemetry**: RSSI, band, channel, SSID and PHY rates from `netsh` (Windows, locale-tolerant), `iw` / `/proc/net/wireless` (Linux) and `airport` / `system_profiler` (macOS), used as evidence in Wi-Fi diagnoses.
- **Active Bufferbloat test**: an 8-second on-demand load test compares loaded and unloaded latency and grades your connection from A+ to F.
- **Bandwidth and process correlation** through `psutil`: live Mbps, observed peak, utilisation %, and the top network-consuming process.
- **Graceful probe degradation**: `scapy` raw ICMP → unprivileged ICMP sockets → OS `ping` → TCP handshake RTT.
- **Chaos Engineering mode** that injects realistic faults, so you can watch a full diagnosis even on a healthy network.
- **Incident log in SQLite** with a 30 s anti-spam cooldown, worst-case metric tracking and a one-click **ISP Evidence Report (CSV)**.
- **NOC-style React dashboard** with a live hop topology, synchronised charts, and a resilient WebSocket client (backoff, jitter, watchdog).

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Validated on a real network
chunks.text:
## Validated on a real network

The test suite is not the only evidence. WiFi-Doctor was installed on a Windows 11 laptop (Hebrew locale, 5 GHz Wi-Fi, ISP router) and every feature was run against the live network. These are the measured results, not synthetic ones:

| Check | Result on the real network |
|---|---|
| Physical Wi-Fi telemetry (`netsh`, Hebrew Windows) | SSID, **−72 to −79 dBm**, 5 GHz ch 40, 802.11ac, 97.5 Mbps PHY rate parsed correctly |
| Adaptive baselines | Learned gateway 3–4 ms, WAN 8–9 ms, DNS 9–11 ms; z-scores near 0 when healthy |
| Bufferbloat test (3 independent runs) | Grade **C** every time: +71 / +105 / +107 ms under 51–83 Mbps of load |
| All four chaos modes, switched back-to-back | 4/4 correct root cause (LOCAL_WIFI 99 %, ISP_WAN, DNS_SERVER 94 %, BUFFERBLOAT) |
| Concurrency guards | Second test → `409`, test during chaos → `409`, chaos during test → `409` |
| Incident log / ISP CSV | Self-inflicted test load creates **no** incident; "real only" export excludes all simulated rows |

The diagnosis for that laptop was consistent across every tool: a weak signal (−77 dBm) and a router without queue management. The Wi-Fi badge, the gateway latency under load and the grade all pointed to the same fix.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Validated on a real network › Bugs that only real-world testing found
chunks.text:
### Bugs that only real-world testing found

Every one of these passed CI and was caught only by running the app on real hardware. Each now has a regression test.

1. **One lost ping raised a Wi-Fi alarm.** On a weak link, 1 dropped probe in a 20-probe window is 5 %, which is over the 3 % threshold. Loss triggers now require at least 2 lost probes.
2. **Back-to-back chaos modes were misdiagnosed** (ISP loss reported as Wi-Fi), because the previous scenario's samples were still in the rolling window. Windows now reset on every mode change.
3. **The bufferbloat test logged an incident against itself,** and its loaded RTTs leaked into the "normal" baseline. Self-induced load is now excluded from incidents and baselines, and the windows are cleared when a test ends.
4. **Closing the console left the backend running,** so the next launch silently served the old version. The backend is now attached to the console window.
5. **The launcher stopped another app's processes.** It found Docker Desktop on port 8000 and killed it. The launcher now stops only its own Python/Node processes and moves to free ports when another program holds 8000 or 5173.

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix
chunks.text:
## RCA Decision Matrix

The verdict is based on a short "recent" view: the median of the last 8 good RTTs and the loss over the last 20 probes (30 s). This lets it react within seconds without flapping on a single outlier. The dashboard still shows full 60-sample (90 s) statistics. Rules are evaluated top to bottom, and the first match wins.

| # | Layer | Trigger (thresholds) | Diagnosis | Recommended remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `LOCAL_WIFI` (CRITICAL) | 100 % WAN loss **and** gateway unreachable | Network link down | Check Wi-Fi association / cable, power-cycle router & modem |
| 1 | `BUFFERBLOAT` | (Gateway RTT **> 40 ms** OR WAN RTT **> 100 ms**) **AND** link utilisation **> 70 %** of observed peak | Local bandwidth saturation (bufferbloat) | Pause/limit the bulk transfer (top process is named), enable **SQM (fq_codel / CAKE)** at ~90 % of plan speed, QoS |
| 2 | `LOCAL_WIFI` | Gateway RTT **> 35 ms** OR gateway loss **> 3 %**, while local traffic **< 15 Mbps** | Wi-Fi signal degradation or router congestion | Move closer, switch to 5/6 GHz, change channel, reboot router, confirm with Ethernet |
| 3 | `ISP_WAN` | Gateway healthy (**< 15 ms, 0 % loss**) BUT WAN RTT **> 120 ms** OR WAN loss **> 3 %** | ISP backbone congestion or upstream routing issue | Power-cycle modem/ONT, check ISP status page, **export ISP Evidence Report** and open a ticket |
| 4 | `DNS_SERVER` | Gateway & WAN healthy BUT DNS resolution **> 150 ms** OR failing (> 3 % timeouts) | Slow / unresponsive DNS resolver | Switch to `1.1.1.1` / `8.8.8.8` on the device or router DHCP |
| 5 | `NONE` | All layers within thresholds | All network layers healthy | No action needed |

**Severity:** `CRITICAL` when loss is ≥ 10 % or latency exceeds the critical threshold for that hop (Gateway 100 ms · WAN 300 ms · DNS 500 ms). Otherwise `WARNING`.

**Confidence score (0–99):** combines *how far* the metrics exceed their thresholds, *how cleanly* the other layers isolate the fault (for example, a clean gateway raises confidence in an ISP verdict), and *how many samples* support it. Weaker fallback branches (such as a degraded gateway under moderate load) are scored lower on purpose.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix › Adaptive baselines (hybrid triggering)
chunks.text:
### Adaptive baselines (hybrid triggering)

Static thresholds remain the hard guardrails. In addition, every hop keeps a rolling buffer of its last **400 good samples** (`BASELINE_WINDOW_SIZE`, ~10 min). From it the analyzer computes a **robust z-score** for the recent RTT median:

```
z = (recent_median - baseline_median) / max(1.4826 × MAD, 1 ms)
```

A hop is flagged as an **anomaly** when the baseline has at least **60 samples**, **z > 3.5**, and the RTT is above a noise floor (gateway 15 ms, WAN 35 ms, DNS 45 ms). Anomalies feed the same decision tree as static breaches, add to the confidence score in proportion to z, and are reported as `WARNING` unless a static critical threshold is also crossed. Chaos-simulated samples never enter the baseline, samples taken during an anomaly are throttled (1 in 10), and the baseline resets when the gateway or resolver changes. The dashboard shows *"Normal baseline: 12 ms (Z: +8.4)"* under each hop.

### Physical-layer evidence

When `LOCAL_WIFI` fires and the radio is weak (RSSI **< −72 dBm**) or on **2.4 GHz**, the diagnosis cites it directly: *"Weak Wi-Fi signal (−78 dBm) on 2.4 GHz channel 6: switch to 5 GHz or move closer to the router."* The confidence score also rises, because the physical measurement backs up the latency evidence. On Windows 11 24H2+, `netsh` needs **Location services** turned on to report Wi-Fi details; without them the dashboard says so, and the RCA uses latency only.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix › Bufferbloat grade
chunks.text:
### Bufferbloat grade

| Latency increase under load | < 5 ms | < 30 ms | < 60 ms | < 200 ms | < 400 ms | ≥ 400 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Grade** | A+ | A | B | C | D | F |

Grades C–F include an SQM/QoS recommendation. The test runs 3 streaming downloads and 1 upload against Cloudflare's speed-test endpoints (with fallbacks) for 8 s while the prober keeps measuring. Only one test can run at a time (HTTP **409** otherwise, also while a chaos simulation is active), and a 10 s watchdog aborts any test that overruns.

**Edge cases handled:**

- A gateway that never answers ICMP while the Internet works is treated as *filtering probes*, not as a fault.
- Peak bandwidth has a 10 Mbps floor, so an idle machine never looks "saturated".
- If ICMP is silently filtered on the network but UDP/DNS works, the prober switches itself to TCP-handshake RTT.

Every threshold lives in [`backend/app/config.py`](backend/app/config.py), and each one can be overridden with an environment variable (for example `GATEWAY_WARN_MS=50`).

---

## Quickstart

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Option A: Docker Compose (one command)
chunks.text:
### Option A: Docker Compose (one command)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yakov-ashgar27/wifi-doctor.git
cd wifi-doctor
docker compose up --build
```

After the containers are up, open:

- Dashboard: `http://localhost:3088`
- API docs (Swagger): `http://localhost:8088/docs`

The Docker setup uses host ports 3088 and 8088, which are uncommon, so it does not collide with other local projects that already use 3000 or 8000.

> **Networking note:** with the default bridge network, *Hop 1* measures the Docker bridge gateway rather than your Wi-Fi router. On **Linux**, use the host-network override to diagnose your real Wi-Fi:
>
> ```bash
> docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.host.yml up --build
> ```
>
> On Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows), run the backend locally (Option B) for true Wi-Fi diagnostics, or set `GATEWAY_IP=<your router>` in `docker-compose.yml`.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Option B: Local execution
chunks.text:
### Option B: Local execution

**Requirements:** Python **3.13** and Node.js **20+**.

**Linux / macOS**

```bash
./scripts/run_local.sh            # unprivileged: icmp_dgram / ping fallback
sudo ./scripts/run_local.sh       # optional: enables scapy raw-socket ICMP
```

**Windows: one click**

Double-click **`scripts\run_local.bat`**. The launcher:

- installs Python and Node.js with `winget` if they are missing
- creates the virtualenv and installs dependencies
- picks free ports if another app (such as a Docker project) holds 8000 or 5173
- opens the dashboard

Keep its window open; closing it stops WiFi-Doctor.

```powershell
# equivalent from a PowerShell prompt
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\run_local.ps1
```

> On Windows, scapy needs [Npcap](https://npcap.com/) and an Administrator shell. Without them, WiFi-Doctor automatically uses `ping.exe` and keeps measuring real latency. On Windows 11 24H2+, turn on **Location services** so `netsh` can report Wi-Fi signal details.

**Manual setup**

```bash
# Terminal 1: backend
cd backend
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

# Terminal 2: frontend
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api and /ws to :8000)
```

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Try the RCA engine in 10 seconds
chunks.text:
### Try the RCA engine in 10 seconds

1. Open the dashboard and wait for the verdict to read **All network layers healthy**.
2. Click **Simulate ISP Loss**. Within a few ticks the WAN node turns red, the latency chart spikes, and the verdict becomes **ISP backbone congestion** with high confidence.
3. Click **Normal**. The incident closes in the history table with its duration and worst-case metrics.
4. Click **Download ISP Evidence Report (CSV)**.
5. With the simulation on **Normal**, click **Run Bufferbloat Test (8s)** to grade your real connection under load.
6. Try **Simulate Wi-Fi Lag**. The gateway badge switches to a weak 2.4 GHz signal, and the diagnosis cites the physical evidence.

Simulated incidents are flagged (🧪 in the UI, `simulated=yes` in the CSV). Tick **Real incidents only** to keep them out of the report you send to your ISP.

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › API reference
chunks.text:
## API reference

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WS` | `/ws` | Live stream: `snapshot` (last 80 frames on connect), `telemetry` (every tick, now with per-hop `baseline_median_ms` / `z_score` and a `wifi` block), `incident` (opened/updated/closed), `chaos`, `stress_test` |
| `GET` | `/api/status` | Latest frame, network info, uptime, connected clients |
| `GET` | `/api/incidents?page=1&page_size=10&real_only=false&layer=ISP_WAN` | Paginated incident history |
| `GET` | `/api/incidents/export?real_only=true` | Streamed CSV evidence report (formula-injection safe, Excel-friendly BOM) |
| `GET` | `/api/chaos` | Current fault-injection mode |
| `POST` | `/api/chaos/{mode}` | `none` · `wifi_lag` · `isp_loss` · `dns_slowdown` · `bufferbloat` |
| `POST` | `/api/stress-test/start` | Start the 8 s bufferbloat test (`202`; `409` if one is running or chaos is active) |
| `GET` | `/api/stress-test/status` | Progress, live Mbps and the graded result |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | Liveness probe |

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Probe reliability (fallback chain)
chunks.text:
## Probe reliability (fallback chain)

| Priority | Backend | Needs | Used when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scapy` raw ICMP | root / `CAP_NET_RAW` / Admin + Npcap | Most accurate, using kernel packet timestamps |
| 2 | `icmp_dgram` | Linux `ping_group_range` or macOS | Unprivileged ICMP sockets, no subprocess cost |
| 3 | `subprocess` | OS `ping` binary | Stock Windows; RTT parsed by a locale-tolerant regex |
| 4 | `tcp` | nothing | Locked-down containers. Times the TCP handshake (SYN→SYN/ACK **or RST**) |

Capabilities are detected at startup. If a backend starts failing at runtime (for example, permissions are revoked), the prober **demotes itself** to the next backend instead of crashing. DNS timing never needs privileges because it sends a hand-built DNS packet over a normal UDP socket.

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Project structure
chunks.text:

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Testing
chunks.text:
## Testing

```bash
cd backend
pip install pytest
python -m pytest -q
```

The test suite feeds synthetic probe streams into the analyzer and checks every RCA branch. It also confirms that each chaos mode is diagnosed as the correct layer with ≥ 70 % confidence. Further tests check:

- the MAD/z-score math and hybrid triggering
- the Wi-Fi parsers, against captured `netsh` (English and German), `iw`, `/proc/net/wireless` and macOS output, including the Ethernet, disconnected and Location-permission cases
- the bufferbloat grade scale, the timeout and offline paths, and the HTTP 409 concurrency guard

API tests need `pip install httpx`.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Configuration
chunks.text:
## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PROBE_INTERVAL_S` | `1.5` | Tick interval |
| `PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` | `1.0` | Per-probe timeout |
| `WAN_PRIMARY` / `WAN_BACKUP` | `1.1.1.1` / `8.8.8.8` | WAN probe targets |
| `GATEWAY_IP` / `DNS_SERVER` | auto | Override auto-detection |
| `PROBE_BACKEND` | auto | Force `scapy`, `icmp_dgram`, `subprocess` or `tcp` |
| `INCIDENT_COOLDOWN_S` | `30` | Minimum gap between new incidents |
| `BASELINE_WINDOW_SIZE` / `BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES` | `400` / `60` | Adaptive baseline length and warm-up |
| `ZSCORE_THRESHOLD` | `3.5` | Robust z-score that counts as an anomaly |
| `WIFI_WEAK_RSSI_DBM` | `-72` | RSSI below which Wi-Fi is cited as weak |
| `STRESS_DURATION_S` / `STRESS_TIMEOUT_S` | `8` / `10` | Bufferbloat test window and hard abort |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/wifi_doctor.db` | Storage |
| `GATEWAY_WARN_MS`, `WAN_WARN_MS`, `DNS_WARN_MS`, `LOSS_WARN_PCT`, `BLOAT_UTILIZATION_PCT`, … | see `config.py` | RCA thresholds |

## Privacy

WiFi-Doctor is 100 % local. It contacts only your gateway, two public anycast resolvers (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`) and your configured DNS server. It has no telemetry, no accounts, and no cloud.

"""Async SQLite engine + session management."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase

from .config import settings


def _ensure_sqlite_dir(url: str) -> None:
    parsed = make_url(url)
    if parsed.get_backend_name() == "sqlite" and parsed.database not in (None, "", ":memory:"):
        Path(parsed.database).expanduser().resolve().parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


_ensure_sqlite_dir(settings.database_url)

engine = create_async_engine(
    settings.database_url,
    echo=False,
    connect_args={"timeout": 15} if settings.database_url.startswith("sqlite") else {},
)

SessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False, class_=AsyncSession)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


async def init_db() -> None:
    from . import models  # noqa: F401  (register tables on Base.metadata)

    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)


async def dispose_db() -> None:
    await engine.dispose()


async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with SessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

chunks.title: analyzer.py › _r
chunks.text:
"""
Telemetry math + Root Cause Analysis decision engine.

Per hop we keep a ``deque(maxlen=60)`` of RTT samples (``None`` = lost probe)
and derive current / average / P95 / jitter / loss. Every tick the RCA engine
walks a deterministic decision tree and emits a structured ``Diagnosis``.

Decisions use a short "recent" view (median of the last 8 good RTTs, loss over
the last 20 probes) so the verdict reacts within seconds and is robust to a
single outlier, while the dashboard shows full-window statistics.

Decision order (first match wins):

  0. Link down          WAN + gateway unreachable                 -> LOCAL_WIFI   (CRITICAL)
  1. BUFFERBLOAT        (GW > 40 ms OR WAN > 100 ms) AND util > 70 %
  2. LOCAL_WIFI         (GW > 35 ms OR GW loss > 3 %) AND traffic < 15 Mbps
     LOCAL_WIFI (weak)  GW degraded under moderate, non-saturating load
  3. ISP_WAN            GW healthy (< 15 ms, 0 % loss) AND (WAN > 120 ms OR WAN loss > 3 %)
     ISP_WAN (weak)     WAN degraded while GW is merely "OK"
  4. DNS_SERVER         GW & WAN healthy AND (DNS > 150 ms OR DNS failing)
  5. HEALTHY
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import statistics
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

from ..config import Settings
from .prober import HOP_DNS, HOP_GATEWAY, HOP_WAN, NetworkInfo, ProbeSample
from .system_monitor import BandwidthSnapshot
from .wifi_stats import WifiInfo

HEALTHY, WARNING, CRITICAL, UNKNOWN = "HEALTHY", "WARNING", "CRITICAL", "UNKNOWN"
LAYER_NONE, LOCAL_WIFI, ISP_WAN, DNS_SERVER, BUFFERBLOAT = (
    "NONE", "LOCAL_WIFI", "ISP_WAN", "DNS_SERVER", "BUFFERBLOAT",
)

HOP_LABELS = {
    HOP_GATEWAY: "Local Router / Gateway",
    HOP_WAN: "ISP / External WAN",
    HOP_DNS: "DNS Resolver",
}


def _r(value: float | None, nd: int = 2) -> float | None:
    return None if value is None or math.isnan(value) else round(float(value), nd)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ stats
@dataclass
class HopStats:
    hop: str
    label: str
    target: str | None
    method: str
    current_ms: float | None
    avg_ms: float | None
    p95_ms: float | None
    min_ms: float | None

    last_ok: bool

    simulated: bool = False
    recent_lost: int = 0

    baseline_median_ms: float | None = None
    baseline_sigma_ms: float | None = None
    baseline_samples: int = 0
    z_score: float | None = None
    anomaly: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


class BaselineTracker:
    """Long rolling buffer of *good* RTTs with a robust (median/MAD) z-score.

    sigma = max(1.4826 * MAD, floor): 1.4826 makes the MAD a consistent
    estimator of the standard deviation for normal data, and the floor stops
    ultra-stable wired links (MAD ~ 0) from turning 0.3 ms of noise into z=10.
    """

    MAD_TO_SIGMA = 1.4826

    def __init__(self, maxlen: int, min_samples: int, sigma_floor_ms: float, admit_every: int = 10):
        self.samples: deque[float] = deque(maxlen=maxlen)
        self.min_samples = min_samples
        self.sigma_floor_ms = sigma_floor_ms
        self.admit_every = max(1, admit_every)
        self._held = 0

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self.samples.clear()

    def compute(self, recent_rtt_n: int, recent_loss_n: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data = list(self.samples)
        ok = [s for s in data if s is not None]
        n = len(data)
        arr = np.asarray(ok, dtype=float)
        # Jitter: mean absolute difference between consecutive successful RTTs
        # (the RFC 3550 inter-arrival idea, without the 1/16 smoothing).
        jitter = float(np.mean(np.abs(np.diff(arr)))) if arr.size >= 2 else None
        recent_ok = [s for s in data[-recent_rtt_n * 2 :] if s is not None][-recent_rtt_n:]
        recent_window = data[-recent_loss_n:]
        return {
            "current_ms": data[-1] if data else None,
            "avg_ms": float(arr.mean()) if arr.size else None,
            "p95_ms": float(np.percentile(arr, 95)) if arr.size else None,
            "min_ms": float(arr.min()) if arr.size else None,
            "max_ms": float(arr.max()) if arr.size else None,
            "jitter_ms": jitter,
            "loss_pct": (n - len(ok)) / n * 100.0 if n else 0.0,
            "recent_ms": float(statistics.median(recent_ok)) if recent_ok else None,
            "recent_loss_pct": (
                sum(1 for s in recent_window if s is None) / len(recent_window) * 100.0
                if recent_window else 0.0
            ),
            "recent_lost": sum(1 for s in recent_window if s is None),
            "samples": n,
            "last_ok": bool(data) and data[-1] is not None,
        }

"""
Active multi-layer network prober.

Hop 1  Gateway   ICMP echo to the default gateway (local Wi-Fi / LAN segment)
Hop 2  WAN       ICMP echo to 1.1.1.1, with 8.8.8.8 raced as backup
Hop 3  DNS       Real UDP/53 A-record query against the system resolver

ICMP backends are tried in order of fidelity and the prober degrades
gracefully instead of crashing:

    scapy        raw L3 sockets (root / Administrator + Npcap / CAP_NET_RAW)
    icmp_dgram   unprivileged ICMP datagram sockets (Linux ping_group_range, macOS)
    subprocess   the OS ``ping`` binary, RTT parsed via regex (works on stock Windows)
    tcp          TCP handshake RTT (SYN -> SYN/ACK or RST) - always available

DNS never needs privileges: it is a hand-built DNS packet sent over a normal
UDP socket, so the measured time is true resolver latency.
"""

return header + qname + struct.pack("!HH", 1, 1)  # QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN


class _DnsProtocol(asyncio.DatagramProtocol):
    def __init__(self, txid: int, future: asyncio.Future):
        self.txid = txid
        self.future = future

    def datagram_received(self, data: bytes, addr) -> None:
        if len(data) >= 12 and struct.unpack("!H", data[:2])[0] == self.txid and not self.future.done():
            self.future.set_result(data)

    def error_received(self, exc: Exception) -> None:
        if not self.future.done():
            self.future.set_exception(exc)


async def dns_query_time(server: str, domain: str, timeout: float) -> tuple[float | None, str | None]:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    txid = random.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
    future: asyncio.Future = loop.create_future()
    transport = None
    try:
        transport, _ = await loop.create_datagram_endpoint(
            lambda: _DnsProtocol(txid, future), remote_addr=(server, 53)
        )
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        transport.sendto(build_dns_query(domain, txid))
        data = await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout)
        rtt = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0
        rcode = data[3] & 0x0F
        if rcode in (0, 3):  # NOERROR / NXDOMAIN: resolver answered
            return rtt, None
        return None, f"rcode={rcode}"
    except (asyncio.TimeoutError, TimeoutError):
        return None, "timeout"
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, exc.__class__.__name__
    finally:
        if transport is not None:
            transport.close()

        self._dns_cycle = itertools.cycle(settings.dns_domains or ["google.com"])
        self._backend_errors = 0
        self._all_icmp_failed_ticks = 0

        await self.refresh_network(force=True)
        forced = self.settings.force_probe_backend
        order = [forced] + [b for b in BACKEND_ORDER if b != forced] if forced in BACKENDS else BACKEND_ORDER
        chain = []
        for name in order:
            ok = await asyncio.to_thread(BACKENDS[name].available)
            if ok:
                chain.append(name)
        self._chain = chain or ["tcp"]
        self._select(self._chain[0])
        log.info("probe backend chain: %s", " -> ".join(self._chain))

    def _select(self, name: str) -> None:
        self._pinger = BACKENDS[name]()
        self.network.probe_backend = name
        self._backend_errors = 0
        self._all_icmp_failed_ticks = 0

    def _demote(self, reason: str) -> None:
        current = self._pinger.name
        idx = self._chain.index(current) if current in self._chain else -1
        if idx + 1 < len(self._chain):
            nxt = self._chain[idx + 1]
        elif current != "tcp":
            nxt = "tcp"
        else:
            return
        log.warning("probe backend %s demoted (%s) -> %s", current, reason, nxt)
        self._select(nxt)

    async def refresh_network(self, force: bool = False) -> None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        if not force and now - self._last_detect < self.settings.network_redetect_s:

def _detect() -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None, str | None]:
            local_ip = detect_local_ip()
            gw, iface = detect_gateway()
            gw = self.settings.gateway_override or gw
            dns = self.settings.dns_override or detect_dns_server(gw)
            return local_ip, gw, iface or interface_for_ip(local_ip), dns

        local_ip, gw, iface, dns = await asyncio.to_thread(_detect)
        if (gw, dns) != (self.network.gateway_ip, self.network.dns_server):
            log.info("network: iface=%s ip=%s gateway=%s dns=%s", iface, local_ip, gw, dns)
        self.network.local_ip = local_ip
        self.network.gateway_ip = gw
        self.network.interface = iface
        self.network.dns_server = dns

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- probes
    async def _ping(self, host: str) -> tuple[float | None, str | None]:
        try:
            return await self._pinger.ping(host, self.settings.probe_timeout_s), None
        except BackendUnavailable as exc:
            self._demote(str(exc))
            return None, "backend-unavailable"
        except Exception as exc:  # never let a probe crash the loop
            self._backend_errors += 1
            if self._backend_errors >= 3:
                self._demote(repr(exc))
            return None, exc.__class__.__name__

    async def probe_gateway(self) -> ProbeSample:
        gw = self.network.gateway_ip
        method = self._pinger.name
        if not gw:
            return ProbeSample(HOP_GATEWAY, None, None, method, "no-gateway")
        rtt, err = await self._ping(gw)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_GATEWAY, gw, rtt, method, err if rtt is None else None)

    async def probe_wan(self) -> ProbeSample:
        method = self._pinger.name
        primary = asyncio.create_task(self._ping(self.settings.wan_primary))
        backup = asyncio.create_task(self._ping(self.settings.wan_backup))
        p_rtt, p_err = await primary
        if p_rtt is not None:
            backup.cancel()
            return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_primary, p_rtt, method)
        b_rtt, b_err = await backup
        if b_rtt is not None:
            return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_backup, b_rtt, method)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_primary, None, method, p_err or b_err or "timeout")

    async def probe_dns(self) -> ProbeSample:
        server = self.network.dns_server or "1.1.1.1"
        domain = next(self._dns_cycle)
        rtt, err = await dns_query_time(server, domain, self.settings.probe_timeout_s)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_DNS, server, rtt, "udp53", err)

"""
Incident lifecycle: turns the per-tick verdict stream into IncidentLog rows.

* Opens an incident when status leaves HEALTHY (subject to a 30 s cooldown
  after the previous incident opened, so a flapping link cannot spam the DB).
* While open, tracks the *worst* metrics seen and escalates severity / root
  cause if a more severe diagnosis appears. Only escalations touch the DB.
* Closes the incident after N consecutive HEALTHY ticks and stores duration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker

from ..config import Settings
from ..models import IncidentLog, IncidentOut
from .analyzer import CRITICAL, HEALTHY, TelemetryFrame

log = logging.getLogger("wifi_doctor.incidents")

_SEVERITY_RANK = {HEALTHY: 0, "WARNING": 1, CRITICAL: 2}


def _max(a: float | None, b: float | None) -> float | None:
    if a is None:
        return b
    if b is None:
        return a
    return max(a, b)


class IncidentRecorder:
    def __init__(self, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], settings: Settings):
        self.sessions = session_factory
        self.s = settings
        self.open_id: int | None = None
        self.open_started: datetime | None = None
        self.last_opened_at: float = 0.0
        self._healthy_streak = 0
        self._peak: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self._severity = HEALTHY
        self._confidence = 0

    async def close_dangling(self) -> None:
        """Incidents left open by a previous crash/shutdown get closed on boot."""
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            await session.execute(
                update(IncidentLog)
                .where(IncidentLog.resolved_at.is_(None))
                .values(resolved_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc))
            )
            await session.commit()

def _merge_peak(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> None:
        for key, value in self._metrics(frame).items():
            self._peak[key] = _max(self._peak.get(key), value)
        top = (frame.bandwidth.top_process or {}).get("name")
        if top:
            self._peak["top_process"] = top

    async def _open(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> dict[str, Any]:
        d, net = frame.diagnosis, frame.network
        self._peak = {}
        self._merge_peak(frame)
        self._severity, self._confidence = d.status, d.confidence_score
        row = IncidentLog(
            started_at=datetime.fromtimestamp(frame.timestamp, timezone.utc),
            severity=d.status,
            root_cause_layer=d.root_cause_layer,
            confidence_score=d.confidence_score,
            title=d.title,
            explanation=d.explanation,
            recommended_action=d.recommended_action,
            gateway_ip=net.gateway_ip,
            wan_target=frame.hops["wan"].target,
            dns_server=net.dns_server,
            probe_backend=net.probe_backend,
            simulated=frame.chaos_mode != "none",
            chaos_mode=frame.chaos_mode,
            **self._peak,
        )
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            session.add(row)
            await session.commit()
            await session.refresh(row)
        self.open_id, self.open_started = row.id, row.started_at
        self.last_opened_at = time.time()
        log.warning("incident #%s opened: %s (%s)", row.id, d.title, d.root_cause_layer)
        return {"event": "opened", "incident": IncidentOut.model_validate(row).model_dump(mode="json")}

    async def _update(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        d = frame.diagnosis
        self._merge_peak(frame)
        escalate = _SEVERITY_RANK[d.status] > _SEVERITY_RANK[self._severity] or (
            d.status == self._severity and d.confidence_score >= self._confidence + 10
        )
        if not escalate:
            return None
        self._severity, self._confidence = d.status, d.confidence_score
        values = {
            "severity": d.status,
            "root_cause_layer": d.root_cause_layer,
            "confidence_score": d.confidence_score,
            "title": d.title,
            "explanation": d.explanation,
            "recommended_action": d.recommended_action,
            **self._peak,
        }
        if frame.chaos_mode != "none":
            values.update(simulated=True, chaos_mode=frame.chaos_mode)
        row = await self._write(values)
        return {"event": "updated", "incident": row} if row else None

        values = {"resolved_at": now, "duration_s": round((now - started).total_seconds(), 1), **self._peak}
        row = await self._write(values)
        log.info("incident #%s resolved after %.0fs", self.open_id, values["duration_s"])
        self.open_id = None
        self.open_started = None
        self._healthy_streak = 0
        self._severity = HEALTHY
        return {"event": "closed", "incident": row} if row else None

    async def _write(self, values: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            await session.execute(update(IncidentLog).where(IncidentLog.id == self.open_id).values(**values))
            await session.commit()
            row = (await session.execute(select(IncidentLog).where(IncidentLog.id == self.open_id))).scalar_one_or_none()
            return IncidentOut.model_validate(row).model_dump(mode="json") if row else None

"""
Chaos Engineering / Fault Injection.

The simulator sits between the real probes and the Analyzer. Real
measurements keep flowing; the active fault is layered *on top* of them, the
way a real fault would add delay or drop packets on one segment of the path.
Faults ramp in over ~3 ticks so charts show a realistic onset rather than a
step function.

Modes
-----
none          pass-through
wifi_lag      +40..160 ms and 8 % loss on the first hop (inherited by WAN & DNS)
isp_loss      +110..260 ms and 18 % loss beyond the gateway (WAN, and DNS rides on it)
dns_slowdown  +220..900 ms resolver latency and 12 % DNS timeouts
bufferbloat   synthetic ~95 % link saturation + queueing delay on every hop
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import time
from dataclasses import replace
from enum import Enum

from .prober import HOP_DNS, HOP_GATEWAY, HOP_WAN, ProbeSample
from .system_monitor import BandwidthSnapshot
from .wifi_stats import WifiInfo


class ChaosMode(str, Enum):
    NONE = "none"
    WIFI_LAG = "wifi_lag"
    ISP_LOSS = "isp_loss"
    DNS_SLOWDOWN = "dns_slowdown"
    BUFFERBLOAT = "bufferbloat"


class ChaosSimulator:
    RAMP_TICKS = 3
    # Synthetic link used for the bufferbloat scenario (Mbps)
    SIM_LINK_DOWN = 100.0
    SIM_LINK_UP = 20.0

        self.since: float | None = None

        self._rng = random.Random(seed)

        mode = ChaosMode(mode)
        if mode != self.mode:
            self.mode = mode
            self.since = time.time() if mode != ChaosMode.NONE else None
            self._ticks = 0
        return self.mode

"""
Active Bufferbloat stress test: loaded vs. unloaded latency.

1. The unloaded baseline is the average gateway/WAN RTT from the last 5
   ticks before the test starts.
2. Concurrent streaming downloads (and an upload) saturate the link for
   ``stress_duration_s`` (8 s) while the normal 1.5 s prober keeps measuring.
3. Latency measured *under load* is compared to the baseline. The inflation
   is graded with the usual bufferbloat scale:

       < +5 ms A+ | < +30 ms A | < +60 ms B | < +200 ms C | < +400 ms D | else F

Safety: one run at a time (``StressTestBusy`` -> HTTP 409), a strict
``stress_timeout_s`` (10 s) watchdog, and transfer workers that stop at the
next chunk boundary. Networking uses only the standard library (urllib in
worker threads), so the test adds no dependencies and never blocks the loop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import itertools
import logging
import threading
import time

GRADE_SCALE: list[tuple[float, str]] = [(5, "A+"), (30, "A"), (60, "B"), (200, "C"), (400, "D")]


def grade_for_inflation(inflation_ms: float | None) -> str:
    """Map latency increase under load to a bufferbloat grade."""
    if inflation_ms is None:
        return "F"  # every probe under load was lost: as bad as it gets
    for limit, grade in GRADE_SCALE:
        if inflation_ms < limit:
            return grade
    return "F"


def needs_sqm(grade: str) -> bool:
    return grade in ("C", "D", "F")

def _median_p95(values: list[float | None]) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    vals = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    if not vals:
        return None, None
    arr = np.asarray(vals, dtype=float)
    return float(np.median(arr)), float(np.percentile(arr, 95))


def compute_result(
    unloaded: list[_Sample],
    loaded: list[_Sample],
    peak_down: float,
    peak_up: float,
    bytes_down: int,
    bytes_up: int,
    endpoint: str | None,
) -> StressTestResult:
    """Pure function: grade a finished test (unit-tested directly)."""
    un_gw = _avg([s.gateway for s in unloaded])
    un_wan = _avg([s.wan for s in unloaded])
    gw_med, gw_p95 = _median_p95([s.gateway for s in loaded])
    wan_med, wan_p95 = _median_p95([s.wan for s in loaded])

    # Internet latency is the user-facing number; fall back to the gateway.
    ref = "wan"
    base, under = un_wan, wan_med
    if base is None or (under is None and gw_med is not None):
        ref, base, under = "gateway", un_gw, gw_med

    lost = sum(1 for s in loaded if (s.wan if ref == "wan" else s.gateway) is None)
    inflation = max(0.0, under - base) if (under is not None and base is not None) else None
    multiplier = (under / base) if (under is not None and base and base > 0) else None
    if not loaded or base is None:
        grade = "?"  # not enough data to grade honestly
    else:

    async def start(self, chaos_active: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        async with self._lock:
            if self.running:
                raise StressTestBusy("A bufferbloat test is already running.")
            if chaos_active:
                raise StressTestBusy("Disable the chaos simulation before running a real stress test.")
            unloaded = [self._sample(f) for f in self._frames()[-5:]]
            self._run = _RunState(uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], time.time(), time.monotonic(), unloaded)
            self.state, self.progress, self.result, self.error, self.finished_at = "running", 0.0, None, None, None
            self.diagnostics = []
            self.live_download_mbps = self.live_upload_mbps = 0.0
            self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._execute(), name="bufferbloat-test")
        await self._emit()
        return self.status()

    def on_frame(self, frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Called by the telemetry loop every tick; keeps the samples taken under load."""
        run = self._run
        if not self.running or run is None:
            return
        if time.monotonic() - run.started_mono >= self.warmup_s:
            run.loaded.append(self._sample(frame))

    async def wait(self) -> None:
        if self._task:
            await asyncio.shield(self._task)

    async def shutdown(self) -> None:
        if self._task and not self._task.done():
            self._task.cancel()
            try:
                await self._task
            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
                pass

    async def _drive(self, counters: TransferCounters, peaks: dict[str, float]) -> None:
        assert self._run is not None
        start = self._run.started_mono
        window: deque[tuple[float, int, int]] = deque()
        while True:
            now = time.monotonic()
            elapsed = now - start
            down, up = counters.snapshot()
            window.append((now, down, up))
            while window and now - window[0][0] > 1.0:
                window.popleft()
            if len(window) >= 2 and window[-1][0] > window[0][0]:
                span = window[-1][0] - window[0][0]
                self.live_download_mbps = (window[-1][1] - window[0][1]) * 8 / 1e6 / span
                self.live_upload_mbps = (window[-1][2] - window[0][2]) * 8 / 1e6 / span
                if span >= 0.45:
                    peaks["down"] = max(peaks["down"], self.live_download_mbps)
                    peaks["up"] = max(peaks["up"], self.live_upload_mbps)
            self.progress = min(1.0, elapsed / self.duration_s)
            await self._emit()
            if elapsed >= self.duration_s:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(min(0.5, max(0.05, self.duration_s - elapsed)))

"""
Local bandwidth & process monitor.

* Throughput (Mbps) from ``psutil.net_io_counters`` deltas on the active NIC.
* Observed peak bandwidth over a ~10 minute window (used for bufferbloat
  utilisation), floored so an idle host never looks "saturated".
* Best-effort "top network process": processes owning live Internet sockets,
  ranked by their I/O rate. Every OS restricts this differently, so every
  ``AccessDenied`` / ``NoSuchProcess`` is handled and the feature simply
  degrades to connection counts (or ``None``) instead of failing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os

def parse_proc_wireless(text: str, interface: str | None = None) -> WifiInfo:
    """Parse ``/proc/net/wireless`` (signal level only)."""
    info = WifiInfo(interface=interface, source="proc")
    for line in (text or "").splitlines()[2:]:
        if ":" not in line:
            continue
        name, rest = line.split(":", 1)
        name = name.strip()
        if interface and name != interface:
            continue
        parts = rest.split()
        if len(parts) >= 3:
            level = _num(parts[2])
            if level is not None:
                level = int(level)
                # Old drivers report 0..255 unsigned
                info.rssi_dbm = level - 256 if level > 0 else level
            info.interface = name
            info.is_wireless = True
            return info
    info.error = "no wireless interface"
    return info


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- macOS
def parse_airport(text: str) -> WifiInfo:
    """Parse legacy ``airport -I`` output (removed in macOS 14.4+)."""
    info = WifiInfo(source="airport")
    values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
        if ":" in line:
            k, v = line.split(":", 1)
            values[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    if not values or values.get("AirPort", "").lower() == "off" or "SSID" not in values:
        info.error = "not connected"
        return info

"""Chaos control + live status endpoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request

from ..engine.simulator import ChaosMode
from ..models import ChaosState

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["control"])

MODES = [m.value for m in ChaosMode]


def _service(request: Request):
    return request.app.state.service


@router.get("/chaos", response_model=ChaosState)
async def get_chaos(request: Request) -> ChaosState:
    sim = _service(request).simulator
    return ChaosState(mode=sim.mode.value, since=sim.since, available=MODES)


@router.post("/chaos/{mode}", response_model=ChaosState)
async def set_chaos(mode: str, request: Request) -> ChaosState:
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"Unknown chaos mode '{mode}'. Use one of: {', '.join(MODES)}")
    service = _service(request)
    if mode != "none" and service.stress.running:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="A bufferbloat stress test is running; wait for it to finish.")
    if service.simulator.mode.value != mode:
        # Rolling windows still hold the previous scenario's synthetic samples;
        # start clean so each verdict reflects only the current mode (baselines are kept).
        service.analyzer.reset()
    service.simulator.set_mode(mode)
    await service.broadcast({"type": "chaos", "mode": mode, "since": service.simulator.since})
    return ChaosState(mode=mode, since=service.simulator.since, available=MODES)


@router.get("/status")
async def status(request: Request) -> dict:
    service = _service(request)
    return {
        "app": "WiFi-Doctor",
        "uptime_s": round(time.time() - service.started_at, 1),
        "clients": len(service.clients),
        "chaos_mode": service.simulator.mode.value,
        "network": service.prober.network.to_dict(),
        "wifi": service.monitor.wifi.to_dict() if service.monitor.wifi else None,
        "stress_test": service.stress.status(),
        "latest": service.latest,
    }
